user_query: What explanation is given for why LINE performed worse than expected in PASSAGE A, and why does LINE(2nd) outperform DeepWalk on the DBLP(PaperCitation) network in PASSAGE B?
llm_response: In PASSAGE A, LINE is said to perform worse than expected because it is a first-order proximity method, so it mainly preserves direct edge relationships and does not capture the richer higher-order structure that helps on the evaluated tasks. In PASSAGE B, LINE(2nd) outperforms DeepWalk on DBLP(PaperCitation) because the paper-citation graph is a directed, weighted network where second-order proximity better preserves the asymmetric neighborhood/citation context, while DeepWalk is designed for unweighted, undirected random-walk co-occurrence and is less suited to that setting.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This answer reflects the standard explanations given for LINE’s first-order limitation and LINE(2nd)’s advantage on directed weighted citation graphs, but I cannot verify the exact wording of the two passages.
